candidate.title: MALBAC
candidate.scope: The assigned MALBAC (Multiple Annealing and Looping-Based Amplification Cycles) genomic-DNA whole-genome preamplification schematic, from Genome through PCR to DNA. Visible inventory: Genome; 27-bp common sequence / 8 random nucleotides; Hybridize primers; Bst DNA polymerase; Denature; Partial amplicons and Template; Cycles of quasilinear amplification with Hybridize primers / Synthesis / Denature; Looped full amplicons; PCR; DNA. The original single-cell DNA implementation is clarified by Zong et al. The MDA/IMS-MDA/MIDAS row above, nuc-seq/SNES row below, clipped STR headings and right-side chemical structures are neighboring context, with no arrow joining the MALBAC route. There are no depicted alternative MALBAC target workflows. The two cycle substrates are represented by separate local operations without asserting separate reaction vessels, specimen pooling or equivalence to neighboring methods. The endpoint is amplified genomic DNA for downstream sequencing, before unshown library construction. RNA/cDNA adaptations, DR-Seq, optimized neuronal RC-seq and comparison pipelines cited in supporting sources are outside this assigned scope.

method_scopes.rationale: All operations belong to the connected row explicitly labeled MALBAC. The graph expands one representative pass through the displayed cycle: copying partials makes full amplicons, whereas copying genomic strands makes additional partials. Distinct output-state IDs preserve each material preparation history. The remaining finite repetitions are contained in o_repeat_cycles, which retains both routes and the already formed full products. This gives an acyclic graph while preserving the diagram cycle. Substrate classes are graph boundaries, not asserted separate vessels, physical pooling, or purification. The Denature/looping interface is compressed in the poster and resolved by primary Figure 1. Initial genomic melting and the common-sequence PCR primers clarify broad drawn interfaces. Bst is retained as the diagram catalyst label, without assigning an identical complete enzyme preparation to every MALBAC implementation. The matching collection page is secondary evidence; its mention of cDNA does not extend the genome-DNA target.
